question: The blue colour of the sky is due to the:
solution:
The correct answer is __**scattering of light.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The blue colour of the sky is due to the **scattering of light**.
 
• The two most common types of matter present in the atmosphere are **gaseous nitrogen and oxygen.**
 
• These particles are most effective in scattering the **higher frequency and shorter wavelength** portions of the **visible light spectrum.**
 
• In physics, scattering is **a change in the direction of motion of a particle because of a collision with another particle**.
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2f7f8975023e2629eafcd7e410ef059ed9fc4a234ce3647a69683d77ae1bbb04.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Refraction of light** is accompanied by a change in the speed of light at the interface of two optical mediums. ​ 
 
• When white light is passed through a glass prism, it splits into its spectrum of colours (**in order of violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange, and red) **and this process of white light splitting into its constituent colours is called as **dispersion**.
 
• Diffraction of light is defined as **the bending of light around corners such that it spreads out and illuminates areas where a shadow is expected**.
